title: Config validation: clarify pool config docstrings + refresh example configs to match Dedicated defaults
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes: Internal-only: Updated pool config docstrings and example configs to match Dedicated defaults; no schema shape changes.
body:
Summary: This PR updates documentation strings (field descriptions) and example pool configs to align with current Dedicated product expectations and what we actually run in new pools. The intent is to reduce operator/customer confusion and prevent “valid but surprising” configs that slip through review, without changing the underlying JSON schema semantics. Context: During the provision-to-ready pilot we saw repeated questions about what defaults are assumed (e.g., autoscaling behavior, readiness gating knobs, region/SKU constraints). We also had at least one edge-case config blocked (INT-1047) where the schema error message wasn’t actionable. This PR focuses on improving clarity: better docstrings, better examples, and tighter “what happens if omitted” language. Not in scope: no new validation rules, no runtime behavior changes, no control plane changes.

What changed (high level): 1) Docstrings/field descriptions: Updated descriptions for common fields to explicitly call out defaults, constraints, and links to runbooks. Improved error/help text for a few ambiguous fields so operators know where to look (e.g., readiness suite thresholds vs routing readiness, and which fields are ignored in certain deployment modes). 2) Example configs: Replaced older sample configs that referenced deprecated helm keys and pre-feature-flag pipelines. Added two examples that match the Dedicated product baseline: (a) “standard dedicated pool” with conservative readiness gates and default autoscaling; (b) “throughput-optimized pool” with explicitly tuned batching/cache + higher canary threshold, intended for internal experimentation. 3) Comments around “Ready semantics”: Clarified that routing only consumes Ready capacity; Validating is not treated as usable. Added inline notes that the perf-canary suite must pass before Ready and how thresholds are interpreted.

Details: - Clarified the following fields (non-exhaustive): pool.region (enumeration + cross-region failover caveat), pool.gpu_sku (naming + heterogeneous restrictions), capacity.min_nodes/capacity.max_nodes (Dedicated defaults + guardrails), bootstrap.helm_chart_version (pinned behavior and rollback note), validation.readiness_suite (what it runs, when it blocks Ready), validation.perf_canary (threshold semantics, units, and where results are stored), routing.advertise_when (explicitly “Ready only”), break_glass (when to use, audit expectations; references ADR-0143).

Changed areas/files (representative): - control-plane/config/schema/pool_config.schema.json (docstrings/descriptions only; no type/required fields changed) - control-plane/config/examples/dedicated/standard.pool.json (new) - control-plane/config/examples/dedicated/throughput_optimized.pool.json (new) - control-plane/config/examples/legacy/pool-minimal.json (updated comments; marked legacy) - docs/internal/dedicated/pool-config.md (synced examples + field table) - control-plane/config/README.md (how to validate locally, links to runbooks)

Illustrative snippet (docstring-only change): Before: "validation": {"description": "Validation settings"} After: "validation": {"description": "Validation gates executed before Ready. NOTE: routing will not use capacity until Ready. Validation includes GPU health checks + networking/TLS + runtime smoke tests; optionally perf-canary. See runbook: Dedicated pool provisioning."}

Testing: - Unit: schema validation tests updated to accept docstring text changes (no behavioral diff). - Local: ran `rwctl pool-config validate` against new examples and a few real configs from staging. - CI: config-schema-tests, lint, and docs build passed.

Rollout/ops notes: - No migration required. - This should reduce repeated questions in #eng-infra during pilots and make review of customer pool configs more predictable. - Follow-up (not in this PR): add a small “common failures” section to the operator CLI output that links directly to the relevant doc section (tracked separately under ENG-2745 comments).

Links: - Linear: ENG-2745 - Related ADR: ADR-0143 (config validation policy gates + break-glass) - Support ticket for messaging clarity: INT-1047
commits: config(schema): expand field descriptions for Dedicated pool configs
config(examples): add standard + throughput-optimized pool examples
docs(dedicated): sync pool-config doc with current defaults
test(schema): update snapshot expectations for docstring text
conversation: Jordan Lee (review): Can you confirm we didn’t change any required fields or defaults at validation time? I’m worried this looks like a behavior change to operators.

Benji Okafor (author): Confirmed: schema shape is unchanged. This PR only touches description/doc fields + examples/docs. I added a note in the summary and double-checked the generated schema artifact diff to ensure no `required`/`default` nodes changed.
Lauren Bishop (review): The example uses min_nodes=2. Dedicated product expectation for new pools is min_nodes=1 unless customer has strict warm capacity. Can we reflect that?
Benji Okafor (author): Updated standard example to min_nodes=1 and added a comment explaining when min_nodes>1 makes sense (strict tail latency / warm standby).
Rafael Mendes (review): Please add an explicit callout that Validating is not routable. We keep having confusion in incident threads.
Benji Okafor (author): Done. Added to schema docstring under routing.advertise_when and in docs/internal/dedicated/pool-config.md under “Ready vs Validating”.
Nina Petrova (review): The throughput-optimized example sets a helm key that was renamed in the pinned chart. Can you update to the current chart value name and mention compatibility?
Benji Okafor (author): Good catch. Updated to the new key and added a small compatibility note under bootstrap.helm_chart_version. Also verified against the pinned chart version used by staging.
Jordan Lee (review): Looks good after changes. Approving.
Lauren Bishop (review): Approved after min_nodes change + comments.
